answer: Each identity stakes a 70-credit bond for one willow post, serial published. Filing costs 31 for the first identity per funding source, rising as 31+5(k-1) for the kth, so the 1000th pays 5026; 1000 fakes pay 2,528,500 plus 70,000 locked. Each epoch it files one whisper-level reading from its copper wire. An auditor recomputes attenuation from the wire-length table; readings beyond 3% or reused across identities burn the bond. A rented-wire ring fails: one serial binds one post/key, so copied copper readings mismatch. An honest identity pays 31 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
